operations.specification: Registration of a new user account, which will be stored in the 'todo_list_users' Prisma table. The request must include an email (unique) and a password, which will be hashed for storage. Upon successful creation, the user will receive newly issued access and refresh JWT tokens, establishing their authenticated session. The 'email' field in the user table must be globally unique; the 'password_hash' field will be generated from the submitted password. This operation enforces minimal retention—user records store only email, hashed password, and administrative timestamps. All initial Todo operations for this user will trace to this newly created account.
operations.description:
This endpoint registers a new user by inserting a record in the 'todo_list_users' table. The primary goal is to securely establish an individual user identity for access to the Todo List application. Client submissions must include a unique email (the request will be rejected if another user already possesses this email) and a password, which is securely hashed and stored as 'password_hash', never in plaintext.

Once registration succeeds, a session is created (referencing 'todo_list_user_sessions'), and JWT tokens are issued. Users are then able to establish session-based access per security and compliance mandates. The newly created account starts with no related Todo items; only minimal account info is retained in the database.

Security best practices are enforced: passwords use entropy-preserving, salted hashing (bcrypt or Argon2), and password policy checks may apply at the DTO validation stage. Only required identity fields are returned by the API—no hashes, timestamps, or internal IDs are ever disclosed.

In the event that the email is not unique, or if the creation fails at any point, the system responds with clear, actionable error messages. Related endpoints include login and token refresh, which use this registered record for their operation.

Error handling covers duplicates (unique index on 'email'), schema validation, and cryptographic exceptions during password processing. Successful registration results in JWT access and refresh tokens, with user ID and role encoded per application policy.

operations.description:
This endpoint performs authentication for a registered user using their submitted email and password. User identity is verified by comparing the supplied email (must exist uniquely in the 'todo_list_users' table) and verifying the submitted password after hashing matches the stored 'password_hash'.

If authentication is successful, session state is tracked in 'todo_list_user_sessions', logging metadata such as IP and origin for compliance and audit purposes. The endpoint returns access and refresh JWT tokens to the client, providing session authentication for subsequent API requests.

Security considerations include strict resistance to timing attacks and leakage—failure responses never disclose if the email or password was incorrect. Inactive or disabled accounts (see 'disabled_at' field) may not log in and will receive a standardized error.

Related endpoints are registration (join) and token refresh, all using the same primary 'todo_list_users' record as their authentication foundation. All failed authentications are logged per compliance requirements.

Errors due to credential mismatch, account suspension, or technical issues are handled in a security-sensitive, user-transparent way. Session records and authentication tokens are issued only on full success.

Session expiry and security logging is enforced based on 'expired_at' and compliance rules.
operations.description:
This endpoint enables users to exchange a valid, unexpired refresh token (issued by a previous login or join operation) for a new access token. It verifies the refresh token's validity and ensures its association with a living session in the 'todo_list_user_sessions' table. Expired or revoked tokens (marked by 'expired_at' in the database) are rejected with clear error messages, enforcing security.

A successful request results in issuance of a new, short-lived access token, maintaining the authentication chain of trust for the session. Token expiration times align with privacy and compliance requirements (refresh valid up to 30 days, access shorter).

When tokens are found to be invalid or the corresponding session record has expired or is missing, the user is required to re-authenticate via the login endpoint. Every refresh operation is logged for auditing. Related endpoints include login (session issuance) and join (initial token grant).

This endpoint never exposes user PII or security-related information related to session status beyond appropriate success or error signals.

Password reset tokens expire based on the 'expires_at' field and may only be used once (see 'used_at'). Issued tokens are suitable for secure delivery out-of-band (such as via email notification). All operations are audited per privacy and incident response policy.

It expects all required business fields, including title, optional description and due date, and a valid status (pending by default). The operation automatically associates the todo with the currently authenticated user and sets system-maintained timestamps for creation and modification. It enforces strict validation rules as described in the schema: title must be non-empty and under 100 characters, description (if present) under 500 characters, due_date (if present) cannot be in the past, and status must be one of the allowed values. Unique constraint on (user_id, title) is enforced; creating duplicate todo titles for the same user is rejected. Soft deletion is supported via status and deleted_at fields but not directly managed by this API.
operations.description:
Create a new Todo task for the authenticated user. This API endpoint enables users to add personal to-do items with business-enforced validation and full auditability.

The API validates the 'title' is non-empty and does not exceed 100 characters as per schema requirements. If provided, the 'description' must be under 500 characters, and the 'due_date' (if given) cannot be in the past. The 'status' field must be 'pending', 'completed', or 'deleted', reflecting the task's current state. Status defaults to 'pending' for new items. On insert, 'created_at' and 'updated_at' are set automatically; 'completed_at' and 'deleted_at' are null. Duplicate titles for the same user are rejected.

Security: Only authenticated users can create todos, and the todo is always linked to the user's own account in the database via a foreign key. All timestamps and ownership fields are managed on the backend to ensure audit trails and data privacy. Related endpoints include updating existing todos and listing user todos.

Security: The endpoint checks current user's ownership of the Todo and never allows cross-user modifications. Errors for constraint violations (uniqueness, missing data, or invalid state transitions) are reported clearly. Related endpoints include Todo creation and list/search operations.

ITodoListUser.IJoin.description:
Join/registration request DTO for creating a new user account in the Todo List application.

This schema is intended for direct client use when registering a new user. Required properties include the core identity fields (unique email and password) and metadata fields collected for compliance, security, and audit trails (session context). Passwords are never stored or returned in plaintext and must always meet system security policy.

Session context fields ('ip', 'href', 'referrer') enable audit logging, compliance investigations, and connection tracing, supporting administrative and forensic processes. Audit metadata is required for user self-registration and is critical for legal and operational compliance reviews. However, these metadata fields may be omitted for admin-initiated user creation where compliance requirements differ.

Validation of all fields is enforced both at DTO and business rule stages (see business requirements for details on length, format, and duplication rules). Email must remain globally unique, and passwords require entropy-preserving complexity per organizational standards.

This DTO ensures that new user registration always creates a parallel entry in the session log table (todo_list_user_sessions) for authentication traceability.

email.description: User's unique email address for authentication and correspondence, as used in the todo_list_users database. Must adhere to RFC 5322 format and is enforced as globally unique per compliance requirements. This field acts as the principal login credential and primary notification destination.

password.description: Plaintext password to be securely hashed by server (bcrypt/Argon2) before storage. The password must satisfy the system's minimum complexity, entropy, and length policies; never stored or returned by API in plaintext form. Required for all user-initiated account creation.

oneOf.description: Client's IPv4 address at the moment of registration, if available. Logged for compliance, security, and incident investigation.
Client's IPv6 address at the moment of registration, if available. Also logged for compliance, security, and incident investigation.
Omitted/undefined if not captured at registration; may be populated server-side from HTTP request context.

ip.description: Client IP address at join. Captured for compliance auditing and session investigation, but may be left null for admin-initiated creation or when the server can infer from the HTTP request environment. Enables precise attribution for forensic reviews.

href.description: Originating client URL (page or source) provided at registration. This helps trace the point of initiation of user creation requests for legal and compliance audits. Required for join flows directly initiated by the user.

referrer.description: Referrer URL at registration, indicating prior browsing or linking context. Aids in compliance and security traceability. Set to an empty string if no referrer is available or provided.

ITodoListUser.IAuthorized.description:
DTO returned when a user is successfully authenticated (registration, login, or refresh). Represents the authenticated session context including issued JWT tokens and core user identity for the Todo List application. Never contains passwords or password hashes. References the session record and grants access according to user role and system policy. Includes user ID for client-side state tracking.

Tokens must be securely stored on the client side for session continuity. The DTO may be used for join, login, and token refresh responses.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated user account. Corresponds to 'todo_list_users.id' primary key field.

email.description:
Unique email address for user login and correspondence.

Email serves as the principal identifier for sign-in and all notification correspondence.
Must be globally unique—accounts with duplicate email are forbidden. Cannot be null or blank.

created_at.description:
Timestamp of account creation (ISO8601, always present).

Represents the instant the account was established. Never changes once set.
Used for auditing, reporting, and data retention purposes.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of most recent account update (ISO8601, always present).

Updated atomically with any profile or status change for the user record.
Essential for auditing changes and synchronization with client caches.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp indicating when the account was administratively disabled (nullable; null means active).

When present, this field indicates the user cannot authenticate or perform actions on the system. Used for both user-initiated deactivations and administrative actions.
If null, the account is currently enabled and accessible.

disabled_at.description: Optional timestamp set when the user account is disabled. Null means active.

ITodoListUser.ILogin.description:
Login request DTO for authenticating a user account in the Todo List application.

Used as the request body to the user login endpoint. Accepts the user's unique email and their cleartext password (which is then securely verified against the stored password hash in the database for credential validation).

Does not accept user ID or any authentication/session context fields (session context managed separately upon successful authentication). Email uniqueness and password requirements are enforced by the backend; raw password is never stored, only compared for secure login.

This schema does not accept system-managed fields (timestamps, account state, etc.).

email.description: Unique email address of the user for authentication. Must match a registered email in the todo_list_users table. Must be a valid, deliverable email address-conforms to RFC 5322.

password.description: Cleartext password for authentication. Must be at least 8 characters and no more than 72 characters (bcrypt safe max). This value is never stored - compared to hash from database. Backend will apply authentication-safe comparison.

ITodoListUser.IRefresh.description:
Refresh request DTO for obtaining new JWT authentication tokens using a previously issued refresh token.

Used as the request body for the token refresh endpoint. Accepts only the current refresh token string originally issued from a prior successful login. All session and device validation is performed server-side.

This DTO accepts only the token string (other session/user context is derived via backend validation; no additional fields are allowed). Never accepts sensitive credentials or system-managed values.

refresh_token.description: The refresh token to be validated and exchanged for new authentication tokens. Must be a valid, active token issued to the current user session. Typically a long, opaque, signed JWT or similar random token.

ITodoListUser.IRequestPasswordReset.description:
Request body schema for initiating a password reset via user email.

This type enables the credential recovery flow by securely identifying the user who intends to reset their password. It validates and accepts a user-provided email address, never disclosing account existence per security and compliance guidance.

Submission triggers generation of a time-limited, one-time-use password reset token. The actual password is never accepted here. Token delivery is handled separately (e.g., via email) following further validation.

All responses—and API behaviors—MUST avoid leaking information about account presence or details. Field-level validation is enforced: email must be in valid format, and improper or missing values must result in generic error handling.

Usage: POST /auth/user/password/request-reset (see password reset endpoint overview).

email.description: The email address of the user requesting password reset. Must conform to the RFC 5322 email format and business validation rules. Entry must be non-empty, unique per user in the todo_list_users table, and trimmed of whitespace before processing. Submission of invalid email addresses results in security-compliant error handling that never indicates if the address exists.

ITodoListUser.IPasswordResetInitiated.description:
Response schema for password reset initiation requests.

Returns an opaque message indicating that the password reset process has been initiated (or at least treated as such). The message is intentionally non-committal to prevent user enumeration or leakage of account details. No token or details about account existence are included — all API responses should be indistinguishable regardless of whether a matching user account exists.

Used in response to POST /auth/user/password/request-reset. This is a business design mandated by the security and compliance requirements for the Todo List application.

message.description: Opaque status message for password reset request. Always a generic string such as 'If an account exists for this email, password reset instructions will be sent.' NEVER includes details about whether the account or email exists, about token delivery, or about success/failure specifics. Example: 'If an account exists for this email, password reset instructions will be sent.'

email.description: Administrator's unique email address. Must be a valid, non-personal business email, used for login, auditing, and compliance purposes. Enforced as unique for admin accounts in the system. Required for registration and future account management.

password.description: Raw password chosen by the administrator for account login, must be at least 8 characters for security. This field is NOT stored directly; will be hashed by the server. Clients must never provide pre-hashed passwords. Password complexity and best practice validation is enforced server-side. Required for registration.

href.description: The URL of the page where admin registration is being performed. Used for session context, auditing, and security monitoring. Required for compliance and forensic trails.

referrer.description: The referrer URL from which the admin registration was initiated. Used for session context, security, and compliance analysis. Required for audit and anomaly detection.

oneOf.description: Optional. IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) of the client performing registration. Used for session and audit context. If omitted, the server extracts it from the request metadata.
Optional. IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) of the client performing registration. Used for session and audit context. If omitted, the server extracts it from the request metadata.
Optional. IP address can be omitted. If not sent, the backend records the client's IP when available.

ip.description: Optional. The client IP address as string (IPv4 or IPv6), or null/omitted. Provided for session tracking, security/audit; if omitted, captured by the backend.

ITodoListAdmin.IJoin.description:
Administrator registration DTO for joining the platform.

Accepts a unique email address, password, and session context fields (href and referrer are always required, ip is optional for audit). The password field should always be provided as plain text for hashing—never pre-hashed. This schema ensures account integrity, security, and unique administrator onboarding. Used exclusively for ITodoListAdmin join operations, not for normal user sign-up nor session management.

Upon success, this triggers the creation of a new admin account in the todo_list_admins table and an initial session record elsewhere. All fields except IP are required for correct compliance and audit trail completeness.

id.description: UUID unique identifier for the admin account. Serves as the primary key in todo_list_admins.

email.description: The admin's unique email address (never null). Returns the current value of the email column for auditing and client display.

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when this admin account was created. Read-only, derived from todo_list_admins.created_at.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this admin account. Read-only, derived from todo_list_admins.updated_at.

oneOf.description: Date/time this admin account was disabled. Null if the account is currently enabled.
Disabled_at is null when the admin account is not disabled.

disabled_at.description: Timestamp or null indicating when the admin account was deactivated (if ever). Used for account state and audit purposes.

ITodoListAdmin.IAuthorized.description:
Response DTO for administrator authentication/authorization.

Returned upon successful registration or login. Provides admin profile details and authentication tokens, omitting sensitive information such as password hashes, which are never included for audit or security reasons.

Enables authenticated access to privileged admin APIs and reveals current account status for audit and UI logic. Passwords and security credentials are never exposed in this schema. 'disabled_at' may be null if currently active.

ITodoListAdmin.ILogin.description:
Login credentials for a platform administrator. This schema gathers the authentication data required to verify admin identity for system access.

An administrator logs in by providing their unique registered email and plaintext password. The password will be hashed by the backend for validation against the admin record in the todo_list_admins table. Email must be registered, enabled, and unique per admin; password is never stored or returned by the API.

Fields for connection context (href, referrer, and ip) are included to record important session metadata for audit, security, and compliance. 'href' and 'referrer' are required for session context logging; 'ip' is optional and may be supplied by the client or extracted by the backend. No additional authentication fields are present, and password is validated against the stored hash. Only enabled (not disabled_at) admins may log in. Session records capture all three context fields for compliance.

This DTO is only used by POST /auth/admin/login and not by user endpoints.

email.description: Administrator's login email address. Must be registered, unique, and case-insensitive. Used as the primary login credential.

password.description: Administrator's plaintext password to authenticate this session. The backend hashes and checks this value against the password_hash field in the database. Never stored or transmitted after initial check.

href.description: Current page URL at the time of login request, provided for session context and audit logging. Required. Example: 'https://todo.example.com/login'.

referrer.description: Referrer URL where login was initiated, for session/usage context and anomaly detection. Required. Example: 'https://todo.example.com/'.

oneOf.description: Optional client IP address, for audit and security monitoring. Typically supplied by the server, but can be provided by client for additional context.
Null if no IP is provided or cannot be determined.

ip.description: Client IP address at login (optional). May be null or omitted; collected for audit/security logs.

ITodoListAdmin.IRefresh.description:
Admin token refresh payload for renewing authentication tokens using a valid refresh token and active session.

The payload contains only the refresh token previously issued during authentication. Validates the admin's session state and credentials by checking token validity in the session record (todo_list_admin_sessions) and corresponding admin status (enabled, disabled_at is null). On success, new tokens are issued and the session record is updated for audit purposes. No credential re-check occurs: only refresh token is validated.

This DTO is only used with the POST /auth/admin/refresh endpoint. User endpoints must not use this type.

refresh_token.description: Refresh token issued during prior admin authentication. Must be valid, not expired, and tied to an active session. Used to renew access and refresh tokens without re-supplying email or password.

email.description:
Registered email address for the administrator requesting a password reset.

Represents the unique login identifier of a platform administrator account. This value must be an enabled admin (disabled_at is null) and correspond to the email field in the todo_list_admins table. Validation will fail if the email is not properly formatted or does not match a registered, enabled administrator account.

Used to initiate the secure password reset process, in accordance with audit and business security requirements.

ITodoListAdmin.IFindForPasswordReset.description:
Request schema for initiating administrator password reset workflow by unique email.

This type specifies the required data needed to begin a password reset operation for an administrator: the admin's unique email address. Upon successful validation, a new secure reset token is generated and tracked for audit purposes.

Only emails corresponding to enabled administrators are accepted; system returns generic responses for unknown, disabled, or non-existent accounts to prevent enumeration.

id.description:
Unique identifier for this password reset token record.

Primary key for the todo_list_password_reset_tokens table entry. Used to correlate audit logs and ensure traceability. Each individual reset token event is assigned a unique value.

token.description:
One-time-use, securely generated password reset token string.

This token must be cryptographically random, unique system-wide, and auditable. It is presented to the admin via secure out-of-band channels (e.g., email, SMS, or other integration). Only valid for the administrator and for a strictly limited time window.

todo_list_user_id.description:
Reference to the user (for admin resets, may be unused or may be set to a system value).

Links to the todo_list_users.id in the primary case, but for admin resets, may either be null or mapped to the affected admin as system context. Included for compatibility with shared flows. Not typically used in pure admin flow, but mandatory for schema completeness.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the password reset token was generated.

Stored in ISO8601 format. Used for audit/compliance tracking and security operations. Required for time-based expiration logic.

expires_at.description:
Timestamp when this token expires and becomes invalid.

Once expired, the token may not be used. Audit/compliance event.

used_at.description:
Timestamp when the reset token was used, if any.

Null if the token has not yet been redeemed. Serves as the marker that the token has been employed for a password reset operation.

ITodoListAdmin.IPasswordResetToken.description:
Response schema for a generated administrator password reset token.

Describes the data structure returned once a valid password reset request for an admin is processed. Includes the secure, auditable reset token, related metadata (creation and expiration time), and references for auditing and system compliance.

The token is returned via out-of-band secure channel (not part of response here), and this schema forms part of the audit trail. Used/expired tokens are not reusable; the used_at field tracks if and when redemption occurred.

id.description:
Primary Key. Universally unique identifier for this user account.

Generated at account registration. Used for all unique referencing of the user entity throughout the system and within the todo_list_users table.
Never changes or re-used once assigned.

email.description:
Unique email address for user login and correspondence.

Email serves as the principal identifier for sign-in and all notification correspondence.
Must be globally unique—accounts with duplicate email are forbidden. Cannot be null or blank.

created_at.description:
Timestamp of account creation (ISO8601, always present).

Represents the instant the account was established. Never changes once set.
Used for auditing, reporting, and data retention purposes.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of most recent account update (ISO8601, always present).

Updated atomically with any profile or status change for the user record.
Essential for auditing changes and synchronization with client caches.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp indicating when the account was administratively disabled (nullable; null means active).

When present, this field indicates the user cannot authenticate or perform actions on the system. Used for both user-initiated deactivations and administrative actions.
If null, the account is currently enabled and accessible.

disabled_at.description: Optional timestamp set when the user account is disabled. Null means active.

ITodoListUser.description:
Registered user account for the Todo List application, as defined by the todo_list_users table in the Prisma schema.

This type includes all profile and account management fields needed for reading or displaying a user's account state.

Sensitive authentication fields (such as password_hash) are never included in this type. The disabled_at field is used to support administrative suspension of accounts for compliance or user-requested deactivation scenarios.

email.description: New unique email address for user login if being changed via account settings. Must remain globally unique across all users. Required only if email is being updated.

oneOf.description: New timestamp indicating when the user account is administratively disabled (ISO8601). Set this to the current time to disable account, or null to re-enable.
If null, remove disabled status and return account to active state.

disabled_at.description: Set or clear the administrative disabled state of a user. Null means re-enable; a non-null date disables the account.

ITodoListUser.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating user account properties in the todo_list_users table.

Allows changing the account email to a new unique value, or administratively toggling the disabled state with the disabled_at field. Cannot be used for changing credentials (password edits require a separate mechanism). All properties are optional and can be independently updated. Security critical fields like password_hash are never present.

ITodoListUserSession.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for filtering and paginating user session records associated with a specific user in the Todo List application.

Admins use this schema to find and review sessions in compliance and security workflows. Combination of filters is permitted, and all parameters are optional unless specified otherwise. Supports searching by IP address, referrer, URL origin, and session timeframes. Pagination and ordering are designed for large-scale audits. Only platform administrators are allowed to use this interface for audit purposes.

ip.description: Filter for matching sessions initiated from a specific IP address. This enables administrators to find all sessions that originated from a particular source, aiding in security incident investigations.

href.description: Filter for sessions initiated from a particular connection URL (origin). Useful for audits tracking location or origin-based accesses.

referrer.description: Filter sessions by referrer URL, supporting investigation of session origination context, including traffic source or platform linkage.

created_from.description: Lower (inclusive) bound filter for the session creation timestamp. Sessions created on or after this date are included in results. Accepts ISO8601 format.

created_to.description: Upper (inclusive) bound filter for the session creation timestamp. Sessions created on or before this date are included in results. ISO8601 format.

expired.description: Boolean filter to return only expired sessions if true, or only active (non-expired) sessions if false. Useful for compliance reviews of session lifecycle.

oneOf.description: Field by which to order session result set. Must be one of: "created_at" or "expired_at". Informs UI sorting and pagination.
Field by which to order session result set. Must be one of: "created_at" or "expired_at". Informs UI sorting and pagination.

order_by.description: Field by which to order session result set. Must be one of: "created_at" or "expired_at". Informs UI sorting and pagination.

oneOf.description: Direction of ordering, either ascending (asc) or descending (desc). Combined with order_by to specify exact result ordering.
Direction of ordering, either ascending (asc) or descending (desc). Combined with order_by to specify exact result ordering.

order.description: Direction of ordering, either ascending (asc) or descending (desc). Combined with order_by to specify exact result ordering.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Used with limit to provide paginated results. Default is 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of session records to return per page. Reduces excessive server load and ensures result sets remain manageable. Maximum allowed is 100. Default may be set by API if not supplied.

ITodoListUserSession.description:
Represents a single, auditable record of an authenticated user session in the Todo List application. Used by administrators for security reviews, compliance audits, and support investigations related to user account access.

Each session tracks the origin of authentication, associated user ID, IP address, initial connection URL, referrer, and timestamps for both creation and (if applicable) termination or expiry. Session events are linked exclusively to one user and cannot be reassigned; linkage ensures full traceability for compliance.

This record is exposed exclusively via admin endpoints and is never modifiable or creatable via direct API calls. Session details are retained for audit, incident response, and system security purposes and do not include personal user data beyond what is strictly necessary for authentication traceability. Any deactivation, expiry, or forced logout is reflected in the session's lifecycle fields, and all access is strictly logged for compliance enforcement.

id.description:
Primary key and immutably unique identifier for this user session in the database.

Used in all audits, trace events, and administrative support cases to reference a specific login instance. Never null or modifiable.

todo_list_user_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the parent todo_list_users entity whose authentication initiated this session.

Links session access records to the user account for full auditability. Used by admins to investigate user-specific access history.

ip.description:
IP address of the client/device that initiated this session. Used for anomaly detection, security event review, and geographic compliance audits.

This field never contains personally sensitive information beyond traceable network metadata. Always populated on successful authentication.

href.description:
URL (origin/context) from which the session was started by the end user (e.g., browser origin or device landing page).

Critical for forensic analysis and security monitoring by system administrators.

referrer.description:
Full referrer URL provided by the client when authenticating for this session. Commonly used to trace navigation flows or identify third-party integrations in compliance scenarios.

Collected at the moment of authentication event creation; never null.

created_at.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601) when the session record was created in the database, i.e., the authentication event occurred.

Present in all session records. Used for reconstructing session timelines during investigations.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601) when the session expired, was terminated, or forcibly logged out by policy or administrative action.

Populated only if/when the session is no longer active.
Null when the authenticated session remains active. Indicates no termination/expiry event has yet occurred.

expired_at.description: Denotes termination of session if completed, otherwise null for still-active sessions.

ITodoListAdmin.description:
Platform administrator accounts for the Todo List application with privileged, system-wide management capabilities.

This schema represents administrators who have full access over all user data, Todos, administrative support actions, and audit/compliance oversight within the system. Each admin account is independently authenticated, managed through unique email credentials (globally enforced), and traceable via all access and update events. No user accounts appear here—admins are never mixed with regular users in the same table by system design.

All administrator account lifecycle events (creation, login, update, compliance/action) are fully audit-logged. Disabling an admin account is supported for incident response or compliance requirements and is recorded via lifecycle timestamps. All authentication and credential management for admins is handled via dedicated password hashing (see `password_hash` in Prisma); this value is intentionally omitted from all returned DTOs for security, following best practices. Only admin actors can access or update admin records via the API, and all such access is audit-logged for compliance enforcement.

This model excludes password hashes and authentication secrets from outputs; inclusion of authentication fields is restricted to tightly controlled contexts only. Review and update activity is always associated with an authenticated admin and fully traceable across system logs.

id.description:
Universally unique identifier (UUID v4) for this administrator account.

This field functions as the primary key for all admin references across the system and appears in every audit record, lifecycle event, or privilege escalation flow. The value is unique, immutable, and assigned at registration. Required for all update, lookup, and audit actions referencing administrators.

email.description:
Globally unique administrator email address, used for authentication, login, audit tracking, and account management flows.

This credential is subject to unique index constraints and is the key identifier for login, account lifecycle audit trails, and system support events. No duplicate, non-compliant, or non-email values are permitted. Used in all privilege escalation or incident response contexts.

created_at.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601) recording when the admin account was created and registered in the system.

Used for system lifecycle management, compliance audits, and to reconstruct event chronology across incidents. Always set upon admin registration; never null.

updated_at.description:
Last update timestamp (ISO 8601) reflecting the most recent administrative change or system-initiated update to the record.

Enables full audit of any privilege change, credential update, or compliance event affecting the admin account. Non-null and updated atomically with each change.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601) when the admin account was deactivated, disabled, or access was suspended for compliance/security.

If present (non-null), the account is not available for authentication and must be handled via recovery or oversight flows. Only set upon explicit disablement.
Null if the admin account is currently enabled and fully active, able to authenticate and operate across the platform.

disabled_at.description: Indicates whether and when the admin account was disabled. Null if enabled, otherwise holds the reasoned system timestamp. Used for lifecycle and incident response controls.

email.description:
Unique admin account email, used for login and audit tracking.

Updates to this field are subject to global uniqueness constraints and full audit logging. Used to identify admin accounts throughout the platform.

password.description: Plain password value for credential reset. This value is securely hashed and stored as password_hash in the database. For compliance, any password reset triggers full audit logging, and raw passwords are never retained after credential update. Only set when updating a password; otherwise, omit or leave blank.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when admin account should be (or was) deactivated for compliance/security reasons.
Indicates the admin account remains enabled. Null by default for active accounts.

disabled_at.description: Timestamp flag to disable the admin account for compliance, incident response, or security controls. Null means still enabled.

ITodoListAdmin.IUpdate.description:
Permitted fields for modifying an administrator account in the todo_list_admins table.

Supports updates to unique email, credential reset, and account enable/disable via timestamp. All changes are logged for audit and compliance. Only administrators may perform these operations. Excludes immutable fields (id, created_at, updated_at) and fields managed by the authentication context. Changes to password are processed via secure hash storage and compliance tracking.

ITodoListAdminSession.description:
Administrator session entity for audit, incident response, and compliance in the Todo List application.

Tracks login sessions associated with platform administrators, each uniquely identified by a UUID and linked to an admin account (todo_list_admins) via a foreign key. Sessions record network and context data (IP, href, referrer), session start/end timestamps, and are used to review access history, security, and incident traces.

Each session belongs to one administrator and may be open (active) or closed (expired). Used for security review, compliance investigations, and platform support. System-generated fields are included as per Prisma schema.

id.description: Globally unique identifier for this admin session. Corresponds to the id field in todo_list_admin_sessions.

admin.description: Reference to the administrator account (todo_list_admins) owning this session. Embeds identity and status (id, email, disabled_at) for complete audit and context analysis. Replaces the raw todo_list_admin_id.

ip.description: IP address for audit, geo-location, and risk tracking. Required for all records. Typically captured from the HTTP request source.

href.description: Session initiation URL for context/audit. Records the requested resource at the moment of login.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page) at session start for anomaly or attack detection. Used to trace sources of login events.

created_at.description: Session start timestamp (ISO8601). Recorded when authentication is successful.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when session was terminated (logout or expire). Null for currently active sessions. Used to determine session validity window.

id.description: Globally unique identifier for this admin session. Maps to primary key of todo_list_admin_sessions.

admin_id.description: Unique identifier of administrator who owns this session. References todo_list_admins.id. Included for context in audit logs.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when session ended, expired, or was terminated (ISO8601 UTC).
Null if session is still active.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when the session was terminated, expired, or ended. Null while active.

ip.description: IP address for audit, compliance, and geo tracking at session start.

href.description: Session initiation URL for context and access traceability. Used in audits.

referrer.description: Referrer URL at session start for anomaly or attack detection.

ITodoListAdminSession.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an administrator authentication session.

Includes session context (ip, href, referrer), lifecycle timestamps, and owner association for audit trails.

References todo_list_admin_sessions; does not expose linked admin detail or session authorization tokens.

ITodoListAdminSession.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for searching/filtering admin session records within a specific administrator context.

Supports pagination, sorting, and search filters (by IP, href, referrer, time range). Used in PATCH /todoList/admin/admins/{adminId}/sessions. All fields are optional for maximal query flexibility. Includes standard page/limit/sort options and filtering criteria for forensic/incident response workflows.

Does not accept direct admin/session IDs (as those are in the path). Only allows filter/search fields and pagination properties.

limit.description: Maximum number of records per page (default/system-capped at 100).

created_from.description: Optional filter: Only sessions created at/after this timestamp included.

created_to.description: Optional filter: Only sessions created at/before this timestamp included.

expired.description: Optional filter: True for only expired sessions; false for only active; null/omitted for both.

ITodoListPasswordResetToken.description:
Password reset token record for secure credential recovery in the Todo List application.

Represents a one-time-use token issued to a specific user, allowing secure reset of account credentials. Every token is a unique record and is strictly time-limited. Includes audit information for issuance (creation), expiration, and usage. Used tokens remain for audit trail but may not be reused. Closely abides by the original Prisma schema and security practices, with sensitive properties visible for administrative or user self-auditing purposes.

This schema is only used for secure recovery workflows and not for login/session routing.

id.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the password reset token record.

token.description: The secure password reset token string. Used for single-use password recovery. Randomly generated and unique.

user.description: Reference to the user who owns this reset token. Derived from todo_list_password_reset_tokens.todo_list_user_id.

created_at.description: Date/time when this password reset token was created and issued to the user (ISO8601 UTC).

expires_at.description: Date/time when this token expires and can no longer be used for password recovery (ISO8601 UTC).

oneOf.description: Timestamp when this token was used for password reset (ISO8601 UTC).
If null, this token has not been used yet.

used_at.description: Date/time this token was used for password reset, if applicable. Null means the token is unused and still active.

ITodoListPasswordResetToken.IRequest.description:
Filtering and search parameters for retrieving password reset tokens for a user in the Todo List application.

Allows searching and paginating password reset tokens, such as by expiration state, date of issuance, usage status, or sorting order. Used for list/review operations and security audits. These query parameters are for list access only and do not affect or modify the tokens themselves.

expired.description: If true, only include tokens that have expired. If false, only non-expired (active) tokens are returned. If omitted, includes both expired and unexpired tokens.

used.description: If true, only include tokens that have been used. If false, only unused tokens. Omitted returns both.

created_until.description: Filter to include tokens created at or before this date-time (ISO8601 UTC).

expires_from.description: Filter to include tokens expiring at or after this date-time (ISO8601 UTC).

expires_until.description: Filter to include tokens expiring at or before this date-time (ISO8601 UTC).

limit.description: Maximum number of tokens per page (pagination). Between 1 and 100 inclusive. Default determined by system.

oneOf.description: Sort field for the list results. Can be 'created_at', 'expires_at', or 'used_at'. Default is 'created_at'.

ITodoListPasswordResetToken.ISummary.description:
Password reset token summary DTO for audit and tracking in API responses.

Returns information about password reset tokens, including identification, associated user, and lifecycle timestamps. Used for administrative/audit listing. Sensitive business details such as raw passwords are never included.

ITodoListTodo.description:
User-created task (Todo) entity representing an individual actionable item in a personal task list.

Each todo belongs to exactly one registered user and records essential details such as title, optional description, due date, and business status (pending, completed, or deleted). Provides complete auditability with timestamps for creation, modification, deletion, and completion event.

Ownership is represented as a reference to the ITodoListUser.ISummary object. All relationships are managed securely by the backend. Writable fields exclude system-managed and ownership fields.

title.description: Todo item title. Required, non-empty text up to 100 characters. Validation enforced on creation and update to maintain business constraints.

oneOf.description: Optional descriptive text (max 500 characters). May be null or omitted if not provided by user.

description.description: Optional descriptive text (max 500 characters). May be null or omitted if not provided by user.

due_date.description: Optional due date for the todo. Must be today or future, if present. Used for sorting and reminders.

ITodoListTodo.ICreate.description:
Data required to create a todo item: title (required), optional description, due date, and initial status. User association and timestamps are handled automatically by the backend.

Field validation follows business and Prisma schema constraints. Status must be one of the allowed values. Description and due_date are optional and nullable as per schema. Audit fields and ownership are managed by the system, not the client.

title.description: New title for the todo. Must be non-empty and under 100 characters. Enforced by business and schema logic.

oneOf.description: Optional new description for the todo. Null to remove; max 500 characters.

description.description: Optional new description for the todo. Null to remove; max 500 characters.

ITodoListTodo.IUpdate.description:
Fields to update for the target todo: new title, description, status, or due date. Only modifiable business fields are accepted. Ownership, audit fields, and user association are system-managed. All fields are optional; only included if changed.

Validation and constraints enforced by business logic and schema definitions.

id.description:
Universally unique identifier for the todo record in the system. This allows precise referencing and auditing of individual todos across internal logs and cross-entity linkages.

Direct mapping to 'todo_list_todos.id' from the underlying Prisma model.

user.description:
Summary information about the owner of this todo item. Derived via the foreign key 'todo_list_todos.user_id', but the raw 'user_id' value is excluded for user privacy.

For privacy-by-design, only a summary of the owning user is exposed; direct user_id is not present in response payloads.

title.description:
Short, required title of the todo item. Must be non-empty, maximum length 100 characters as enforced by business validation and database schema. Allows users to quickly identify tasks in lists and overviews.

Directly maps to 'todo_list_todos.title'.

description.description:
Optional descriptive text (may be null if not provided by the user). Limited to a maximum of 500 characters for validation purposes.

Direct mapping to 'todo_list_todos.description' in database; business logic accepts null for omitted values.

Current status of the todo. Allowed values are 'pending', 'completed', or 'deleted'.

This directly maps to 'todo_list_todos.status' and drives workflow/lifecycle transitions in the API and business rules.

due_date.description:
Optional due date for the todo. Will be 'null' if not set by the user; otherwise, represents a specific due datetime in ISO 8601 format.

Maps to 'todo_list_todos.due_date' in the database, supporting client- and server-side deadline reminders.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601) when the todo was marked as completed by the user. Null if task is not completed.

Direct mapping to 'todo_list_todos.completed_at'. Serves for auditability and completion metrics.

created_at.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601 format) when the todo was created. Immutable field for lifecycle traceability.

Directly maps to 'todo_list_todos.created_at'.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the last update to the todo. This is updated on any change (status transition, field modification, etc.). Aids in tracking modifications and changes for audit and compliance.

Direct mapping to 'todo_list_todos.updated_at'.

deleted_at.description:
If the todo was deleted, this is the timestamp (ISO 8601) when deletion occurred. Field is set to null if the todo is still active.

Maps to 'todo_list_todos.deleted_at'. Used in business logic for soft deletion and retention policy enforcement.

ITodoListTodo.ISummary.description:
Provides a summarized view of a Todo item for public API responses, such as in listing/search or detail endpoints.

Each summary represents a single personal task, showing essential fields and activity metadata (creation, update, status, due date if set, and deletion/completion audit info), but intentionally omits direct exposure of the user foreign key for privacy-by-design. Instead, the 'user' summary is provided for informational nesting, upholding privacy and compliance best practices.

Designed to support list views, search results, and detail displays while remaining safe for third-party or public exposure with all critical state transitions traceable for auditing.

limit.description: Maximum number of items per page; subject to enforcement of API/system policy limits.

ITodoListTodo.IRequest.description:
Schema used for advanced search, filter, and pagination in endpoints for retrieving Todo items. Allows end-users to perform full-text, status, and date-range queries with client-driven paging.

User access permissions and security checks guarantee that only tasks owned by the requester are considered, and all server-side filtering/paging is enforced for privacy and scalability.

APIs using this schema provide consistent pagination and filtering, with maximum per-call limits dictated by backend business logic.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user account. Maps to todo_list_users.id.

email.description: Unique email address for login and correspondence. Maps to todo_list_users.email.

created_at.description: Datetime of user account creation. Corresponds to todo_list_users.created_at.

updated_at.description: Datetime of account's latest update. Maps to todo_list_users.updated_at.

disabled_at.description: If applicable, time when the account was disabled. Null if still active; maps to todo_list_users.disabled_at.

ITodoListUser.ISummary.description: Summary DTO with essential, publicly exposable information about a todo list user. Used for nesting within other summary types and for representing owners in lightweight operations. Excludes sensitive/authentication fields.

ITodoListAdminAuditLog.description:
Administrative action and compliance audit log for critical admin-user or admin-todo interactions.

Represents a single, immutable record in the append-only audit trail for administrative activities over user or Todo data in the system. Each audit log entry identifies the acting admin, the affected user (if any), optionally the specific Todo targeted, a categorical action label, the request context metadata, and exact creation timestamp. This type is used in API responses for retrieving full audit details for compliance, incident review, and administrative accountability scenarios.

All personal data fields (admin_id, user_id, todo_id) reference other tables by UUID, supporting traceability while preventing direct inclusion of business entity information in the audit log structure. Timestamps are required and immutable. The structure is optimized for secure, read-only operations by privileged administrative actors and is never exposed to ordinary users.

id.description: Primary key for the audit log record. Universally unique identifier assigned immutably when each log entry is created. Used for referencing and cross-auditing.

admin_id.description: UUID of the acting administrator who performed the operation. Refers to a valid admin account. Used for traceability of privileged actions.

user_id.description: UUID of the regular user affected by the operation, if applicable. May be null for audit events that do not target a specific user.

todo_id.description: UUID of the target Todo item for the audit event, if applicable. Null if the administrative action does not target a specific Todo.

action_type.description: Categorical label for the administrative operation performed: typical values include 'create', 'update', 'delete', and 'access'. Used for filtering and compliance classifications.

request_context.description: Optional extended, machine-readable metadata describing the admin request environment (such as source IP, session ID, endpoint, or business context). May be null for legacy or minimal log entries.

created_at.description: Timestamp of when this administrative audit entry was created. Set automatically at write time and always reflects UTC. Immutable once assigned.

ITodoListAdminAuditLog.IRequest.description:
Request filter and pagination parameters for retrieving administrative audit logs related to a specific Todo.

Enables API consumers to search, filter, and page through audit events based on action type, administrator identity, affected user, and time range. All search parameters are optional for maximum query flexibility. Used as patch request body in the audit log list/search operation. Supports admin actors only and is never available to ordinary users.

Pagination constraints guarantee no more than 100 entries per page. Business rule: Only logs for the requested Todo and accessible to the requesting admin will be returned.

page.description: Page number to fetch, for paginated search. Must be at least 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of audit log entries to retrieve. Must be between 1 and 100 inclusive.

oneOf.description: The field by which to sort the audit logs. Allowed: 'created_at', 'action_type'.
The field by which to sort the audit logs. Allowed: 'created_at', 'action_type'.

sort.description: The field by which to sort the audit logs. Allowed: 'created_at', 'action_type'.

oneOf.description: Sort direction for returned audit records. Either 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending).
Sort direction for returned audit records. Either 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending).

order.description: Sort direction for returned audit records. Either 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending).

action_type.description: Filter results to only this action type (e.g., 'create', 'update', 'delete', 'access'). Optional. Case-sensitive.

admin_id.description: Restrict results to actions performed by a specific admin (by UUID). Optional.

user_id.description: Restrict results to audit logs that affected this user (by UUID). Optional.

created_from.description: Restrict results to audit logs created at or after the specified date/time (exclusive). ISO8601 format.

created_to.description: Restrict results to audit logs created at or before specified date/time (inclusive). ISO8601 format.

id.description: Unique identifier for this user session record. Corresponds to the primary key of todo_list_user_sessions.

user_id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated user for this session. References todo_list_users.id. Provided for quick association in summary listings.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp of session creation (ISO8601 format).

oneOf.description: UTC timestamp when the session ended, expired, or was forcibly terminated.
Null if the session is currently active and has not yet expired.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when session was terminated or expired. Null if session is currently active.

ip.description: IP address at session initiation. Used for audit, anomaly detection, and context.

href.description: Connection (origin) URL for session at initiation, for audit and traceability.

referrer.description: Client referrer URL at session start. Used for audit and security investigation.

ITodoListUserSession.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a user authentication session in the Todo List system.

Captures both session context (origin, referrer, IP) and lifecycle (creation and expiry times). Used for listings and audit purposes.

References the todo_list_user_sessions table; does not expose linked user or sensitive authorization data directly.

ITodoListAdmin.ISummary.description:
Summary reference for a platform administrator in the Todo List application.

This schema serves as an optimized, minimal identity and state descriptor for admin summary references in related entities (such as session/audit logs or nested relations). It includes only the essential, non-sensitive fields to enable lightweight display as well as efficient lookup, search, and access pattern support.

Designed to prevent circular expansion and data leakage in aggregation scenarios. For full account details, use the ITodoListAdmin schema.

The properties mirror essential columns (id, email, disabled_at) from the todo_list_admins table. Field selection and structure follow DTO-summary conventions and respect all constraints described in the Prisma schema.

id.description: Universally unique identifier for administrator accounts, as generated by the todo_list_admins table. This value is stable for the account lifetime and is the primary cross-entity reference in all user/session/audit relationships.

email.description: Unique administrator account email. This field is used both as a login credential, for deduplication/audit, and as an identity proof in related tables. Must match unique and not-null constraints from the database.

oneOf.description: Timestamp of administrative disablement, as set for compliance or incident response. Represents when the account was (temporarily or permanently) disabled for access control and auditing purposes. Null values indicate the account is currently enabled and active.
No disablement timestamp has been recorded; the administrator is currently active and permitted access.

disabled_at.description: Disabled state indicator and compliance status, derived from the database's nullable datetime column. Null if enabled; otherwise, contains the deactivation/disabling datetime.
